mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate the Federal Reserve will pause rate hikes, thereby boosting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% and FEDFUNDS remains below 5.0% for the subsequent month
regime_hint: preemptive pause in Fed rate hikes
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified trigger window, or CPIAUCSL reverts below 0.3% within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) above 155,000 indicates growing hiring momentum, which reduces expected wage growth and lowers real interest rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS averages above 155,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the labor expansion episode, or unemployment falls below 3.5% during the same window.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 (goods orders) of at least 5% signals weakening business demand, which elevates uncertainty and compresses forward discounting, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines by at least 5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive during the identified GDPC1 decline episode, or the decline is not followed by negative 5-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 coinciding with a sustained rise in RSAFS (retail sales) above 700,000 suggests a structural shift toward services dominance, which elevates equity volatility and lowers 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 and RSAFS rises above 700,000 for two consecutive months
regime_hint: transition from manufacturing to services dominance
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the identified structural shift episode.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4.75% for three consecutive months in a context of falling UNRATE (<3%), it signals persistent tightening and higher real borrowing costs, which predict negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.75% and UNRATE remains below 3.0% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: prolonged Fed tightening with low unemployment
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the trigger period, or FEDFUNDS reverts before the three-month window closes.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in HOUST (housing starts) below 1,400 units followed by a sustained rise above 1,500 for two months indicates a turning from cooling to heating in the housing cycle, which reduces uncertainty and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 1,400 for one month then rises above 1,500 for two consecutive months
regime_hint: shift from cooling to heating in housing market
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified housing cycle shift.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in PAYEMS (employment growth) of more than 2% while UNRATE remains below 4% suggests weakening labor demand, which amplifies recession risk and compresses equity valuations, producing negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines by >2% for two consecutive months and UNRATE < 4% throughout
regime_hint: labor demand weakness in low-unemployment environment
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the identified labor demand episode.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE crosses above 4% and FEDFUNDS remains below 4.5% for three months, it indicates a shift toward a more accommodative policy environment that lowers real financing costs and supports a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.0% and FEDFUNDS remains below 4.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified policy shift.
